sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Miu language (mpo), state of 4 Nov 2025.
sources.note: Catalog only: lists Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List and Throop & Throop 1980; no PARADISEC deposits, no texts, no lexica, no descriptions.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic Languages. Richmond: Curzon (language listing; Kaulong sketch pp.387-409 adapted by Ross).
sources.note: Miu appears in the language listing with no source (undescribed). The Kaulong sketch p.388 gives the only Pasismanua stress statement ('Kaulong stress generally falls on the final syllable of a verb and on the penultimate syllable of a noun') -- Kaulong, not Miu.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page miuu1237 and reference list; sil.org archive search 'Miu'; ABVD Pasismanua node; Wikipedia 'Miu language'.
sources.note: Glottolog: 0 descriptive refs (Chowning 1996 + Ethnologue on page). SIL archives: one hit (39260). ABVD: Kaulong and Sengseng lists only, no Miu. Wikipedia: stub citing Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1996. Relations among languages of West New Britain. In Ross (ed.), Studies in languages of New Britain and New Ireland 1, 7-62. PL C-135.
sources.note: Miu cited for a few lexical/morphological forms (masculine prefix, pronoun wid 'she'); sec. 11.1 phonology has no stress statement.

sources.citation: Throop, Craig (compiler). 1992. Kaulong Organised Phonology Data. SIL, Ukarumpa. 5 pp. (nearest described relative)
sources.note: Kaulong only; 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' heading is empty. No Miu data.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. xiii+487 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing on Miu. Miu appears only as a member of the Pasismanua chain (pp.161-163, 173) and in the informant appendix p.398 (no Miu informant listed). Comparative work, no synchronic prosody for any Pasismanua language.

sources.citation: Thurston, William R. 1987. Processes of change in the languages of north-western New Britain. Pacific Linguistics B-99. Canberra: Department of Linguistics, Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. viii+163 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-B99 (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/145417; text extract).
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number Philol69.57.3 no.99
sources.note: Nothing on Miu prosody. The phonology remarks concern the NW New Britain languages ('All the AN languages of NWNB have a standard five-vowel system. In addition to these, Anem has two back unrounded vowels'); searched stress/accent/tone/penult: no statement touching Miu or the Pasismanua chain. Miu occurs once (text line ~3099 of the ANU extract), as a cited form from Throop & Throop 1980.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1985. Rapid lexical change and aberrant Melanesian languages: Sengseng and its neighbours. In Pawley & Carrington (eds), Austronesian linguistics at the 15th Pacific Science Congress, 169-198. PL C-88.
sources.note: Miu mentioned pp.170-171 (westernmost Pasismanua language, <400 speakers). Phonology remarks (pp.174-179) concern Sengseng segmentals, clusters, vowel dropping; no stress statement for Miu or any Pasismanua language.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Britain. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study vol.2, 365-386. PL C-39.
sources.note: Miu listed as language no. 24 of the Whiteman group; p.379 speculates on 'possibility of phonemic tone in some Whiteman languages'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1969. The Austronesian languages of New Britain. In A. Capell, A. Chowning & S. A. Wurm, Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 2, 17-45. Pacific Linguistics A-21. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: No phonology for Miu or any Pasismanua language: sec. 3.71 (p.32) gives location and membership ('the four dialects that compose the Pasismanua group: Miu, Kaulong (a Kinum), Sengseng, and Karore'), lexicostatistical relations to Arawe, Bao, Kapore; language list and map. Classification survey only.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. n.d. Field notes and draft comparative vocabularies of Pasismanua languages (Sengseng, with Miu and Psohoh data cited in Chowning 1996); possibly in PARADISEC collection AC2 or ANU archives.

sources.note: Chowning 1996 says 'my data for Miu and Psohoh are incomplete', implying unpublished Miu notes; any transcription with stress marks would be the only primary Miu prosodic data.
